articles.body:
The 2026 Presidents Cup is set to tee off Thursday at Medinah Country Club Course No. 3 near Chicago, pitting some of the best golfers from the United States and around the world against each other in an international competition.

The Golf Channel will be providing live coverage for the first two days of the event before NBC and Peacock take over on Saturday and Sunday.

Here's a breakdown of this weekend's schedule for the 2026 Presidents Cup.

Presidents Cup Opening Ceremony, Noon-12:30 p.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 1 Matches- Fourballs, 12:30-7 p.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 2 Matches- Foursomes, 2-7 p.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 3 Matches- Fourballs, 8-9 a.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 4 Matches- Fourballs and Foursomes, 9 a.m. ET-7 p.m. ET (NBC/Peacock)

Final Round Matches- Singles, Noon-6 p.m. ET (NBC/Peacock)

The Presidents Cup pits 12 U.S. golfers against 12 international players from everywhere in the world except Europe. The U.S. has won 10 straight showdowns, most recently earning an 18.5-11.5 victory at Royal Montreal Golf Club two years ago.

Brandt Snedeker is the captain of the U.S. team, while Australia's Geoff Ogilvy is the international team captain.

Fans will be excited to see if the U.S. can continue its dominance or if the international team finally breaks through this year.

articles.title: Aaron Rai and Tiger Woods’ unlikely full-circle story: From old VHS tapes to the PGA Championship winner meeting his childhood golfing hero
articles.summary: Explore the inspiring story of Aaron Rai, who became a PGA Championship winner influenced by his childhood hero, Tiger Woods. Discover how Rai's admiration for Woods shaped his golfing journey and led to his historic achievement.
articles.body: Aaron Rai’s road to major championship glory is linked to Tiger Woods’ influence. Woods was a major influence on Rai growing up long before he became a professional golfer, with Rai and his father Amrik often watching VHS tapes of the American star’s performances.That early fascination became part of Rai’s professional motivation. Years later, Rai met Woods in person, a moment that connected his childhood hero worship with his life as a professional golfer. Then came his win at the 2026 PGA Championship, and another big chapter was added to a story that began with those childhood viewings.Inside Aaron Rai and Tiger Woods’ unlikely full-circle story leading to the PGA ChampionshipAaron Rai was born and raised in Wolverhampton, England, in a family where golf was a big part of life. Amrik, his father, had a big role in developing his son's game, searching for information that could help Rai understand golf technique, particularly the mechanics of the swing.That process became a big part of Tiger Woods. Rai and his father would watch old VHS tapes of Woods, including footage of the American’s historic amateur career and major championship wins. The videos enabled young Rai to learn from one of the sport’s most impactful figures, as well as be inspired during his own development.Rai was studying Woods' three consecutive victories at the U.S. Amateur Championship from 1994 to 1996. Another fascination was the way he dominated the major championships in the early 2000s.To Rai, the recordings were more than entertainment. They were part of his education in the sport and helped shape his understanding of what was possible at the highest level.Tiger Woods connection shaped Aaron Rai’s golf journeyAs his own golf career developed, so did his admiration for Woods. The link took on a special significance in 2013 when Rai and his father went to Muirfield for The Open Championship to try and catch a glimpse of Woods during a practice round.The pair are said to have driven through the night and arrived early in the morning. At that stage Rai didn’t get the chance to meet Woods one-on-one, but the experience showed how big a part Woods played in his golfing journey.A decade later, Rai finally got to meet Woods at the pro-am for the 2023 Genesis Invitational. It was an opportunity for Rai to meet the player he had been following since childhood.Rai also walked the final nine holes of one of Woods’ practice rounds at that tournament. Watching Woods took time away from his own professional golfer preparation routine, highlighting the enduring significance of his childhood hero.The two golfers did not have formal mentorship. Woods’ influence was mainly from watching him, his career, his performances and his approach to the game.That distinction makes the story even more important. Rai created his own professional golfer’s persona, bringing with him lessons and inspiration from a player he had watched for years.Aaron Rai’s childhood inspiration leads to PGA ChampionshipRai’s biggest career achievement came as a breakout at the 2026 PGA Championship. He closed with a five-under 65 at Aronimink Golf Club to claim the Wanamaker Trophy.His final round was also part of an unusual scoring achievement. Rai improved his score in all four rounds, moving from 70 to 69, then 67 and finally 65.His consistency gave his victory a significant historical context. Rai’s victory was the first PGA Championship win for an Englishman since Jim Barnes in 1919 and ended a long wait for an English-born champion at the event.The victory also lent more significance to some of Rai's quirky golfing habits, many of which are tied to his upbringing and his relationship with his late father.Rai is known for wearing two gloves when he plays, rather than the single glove worn by professional golfers. The habit started in his childhood in England, when he would wear gloves on both hands to help him get through the cold conditions during practice.Aaron Rai’s historic win honors his family rootsAaron Rai is also still getting covers on his irons. It’s the same practice as his father’s approach to equipment and sacrifices made to get Rai quality clubs when he was young.Those habits have remained with Rai even as he’s risen to elite professional golfer status. They are a reminder of a previous time in his career, of the family support that helped build his foundation in the sport.MilestoneSignificanceChildhoodRai watched Tiger Woods footage with his father, Amrik1994–1996 footageWoods’ three U.S. Amateur victories became part of Rai’s viewing2013Rai and his father travelled to Muirfield to watch Woods2023Rai met Woods at the Genesis Invitational2026Rai won the PGA Championship at Aronimink Golf ClubRai’s PGA Championship win is thus not like any other standard breakthrough story. One can see several stages in his success, from being exposed to Woods as a child, to years of pro development, to a long-awaited meeting with his idol, and finally to winning a major championship of his own.The symbolism is even more powerful because Woods was the gold standard for the young Rai, and Rai has carved out his own place in the history of major championships.The link does not mean that Woods was the direct architect of Rai’s success. Instead, it shows how one athlete can shape the dreams of another, long before the two ever share the same professional space.From watching Woods on VHS tapes with his dad to meeting him as an established pro, Rai’s story already had a pretty incredible full-circle moment, and the defining achievement was winning the 2026 PGA Championship, turning that childhood inspiration into one of golf’s most memorable personal journeys.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns to partner for first Thursday fourballs match for Team USA
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns will take on Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im as the first group to go out on Thursday's fourballs at the Presidents Cup, as both captains revealed their pairings on Wednesday; watch Thursday's fourballs live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Brandt Snedeker's Team USA are looking to extend their winning streak to 11 consecutive victories over the International team at Medinah Country Club.

Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele head out in match two and will take on Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune.

Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele will head out in match two and will take on Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune.

Snedeker has chosen to pair experienced Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup player Justin Thomas alongside 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun for match three.

They'll take on Canadian Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria of Colombia.

A blockbuster group will go out in the fourth match of the day, with two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa taking on the reigning Open champion Ryan Fox and 2013 Masters winner Adam Scott.

Chris Gotterup will pair with Patrick Cantlay in the final game of the fourballs session against Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim.

Match one will get under way at 5.35pm (UK and Ireland time) with the International team set to take the honours off the tee.

Thursday fourballs and tee times (all UK and Ireland time)

Match 1 (1735): Scottie Scheffler/Sam Burns vs Min Woo Lee/Sungjae Im

Match 2 (1753): Cameron Young/Xander Schauffele vs Hideki Matsuyama/Ryo Hisatsune

Match 3 (1811): Justin Thomas/Jackson Koivun vs Corey Conners/Nico Echavarria

Match 4 (1829): Wyndham Clark/Collin Morikawa vs Ryan Fox/Adam Scott

Match 5 (1847): Chris Gotterup/Patrick Cantlay vs Tom Kim/Si Woo Kim

Scheffler, Burns out to end unwanted streak

Scheffler and Burns have struggled together in past team events, despite being good friends, with the duo having fallen to an underwhelming record of 0-3-1 at the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup.

"Do I think we have unfinished business? I don't know if I would call it that," Burns said.

"It's been frustrating the times we have played together, and we feel like we've played really well and ultimately not won," Burns said. "It's been more frustrating than anything.

"Yeah, this week we're going to go out and compete as hard as we can and try to get as many points for the US team as possible."

Snedeker also delved into his decision to pair up Koivun and Thomas, explaining the decision was an easy one given how well the two pair together.

"Jackson being a young kid, I feel like he's really kind of found his way on our team really quickly," Snedeker said on Wednesday. "I feel like he's handled the adjustment really well. Justin is just a natural pairing for him.

"He's somebody he's comfortable with. He'll do a great job putting his arm around him and show him how USA golf is meant to be played.

"I think we're really excited about all these match-ups and put this line-up out."

Fox taking inspiration from Europe's Ryder Cup stars

Open champion Fox is hoping the International Team can channel the energy of Team Europe at the 2025 Ryder Cup and are motivated to win for Scott.

"For us, we've always been the underdogs in this," Fox said.

"But I feel like on paper the European Ryder Cup team is always the underdogs a little bit, and that hasn't seemed to affect their results at all over the last few years.

"We're trying to channel a little bit of that and come together.

"We do have a chance to do something incredible when we've got a couple of guys on the team who have played a lot of these that we really want to get a win for. That's our motivation. I mean, Adam [Scott] especially over there.

"We're trying to flip the pressure on the US. I feel like they're expected to win, and if we can get on top early and create some pressure, there will be more pressure come on them from other places and hopefully we can take advantage of that."

articles.title: US seeks 11th Presidents Cup win in a row over global foes
articles.summary: United States golfers will try to stretch their win streak to 11 while the Internationals seek their first victory since 1988 when the 16th Presidents Cup be...
articles.body:
United States golfers will try to stretch their win streak to 11 while the Internationals seek their first victory since 1988 when the 16th Presidents Cup begins Thursday at Medinah.

The Americans own a 13-1-1 edge over their non-European global rivals in a biennial series that has failed to produce the drama and tension of the US-Europe Ryder Cup rivalry.

The Internationals' lone triumph came 28 years ago at Australia's Royal Melbourne with a 2003 draw in South Africa their only other bright spot.

The global squad will try to pull off a "Miracle at Medinah" in the footsteps of Europe's 2012 Ryder Cup fightback from 10-6 down with eight wins and a draw in singles for a 14.5-13.5 victory at the suburban Chicago layout.

But they will not be drawing much inspiration from that comeback.

"We really just focus on what we're doing," said Internationals captain Geoff Ogilvy of Australia. "The boys are excited. We all have memories, pretty vivid memories, of watching that Sunday at that Ryder Cup, just as an interested observer.

"We take our own inspirations from our own sort of stuff."

US captain Brandt Snedeker, who won his 10th PGA Tour title in May at Myrtle Beach, had no clue why the Americans could dominate the Presidents Cup yet lose nine of the past 12 Ryder Cups.

"Trying to figure out the secret sauce, if you will, of why the success has been this way is the hardest question we're trying to answer," Snedeker said.

"The makeup of every team is different. The bonding in every team is different. So trying to navigate that is really difficult."

Americans boast eight of the top 11 players in the world rankings with world number one Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Collin Morikawa and Russell Henley plus captain's picks Chris Gotterup and Xander Schauffele.

Other US captain's picks include Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay and rookies Jacob Bridgeman, a winner last week at Biltmore, and Jackson Koivun, a 21-year-old who won the 3M Open in July in only his third professional start.

Scheffler is only 3-5-1 in prior Presidents Cup appearances but Snedeker is not worried about the reigning PGA FedEx Cup champion.

"Scottie Scheffler being Scottie Scheffler is the most important thing for us as a team. We can't ask him to do more than he can do," Snedeker said.

"He can only deliver five points at his best, if he goes out and plays unbelievable. We just want Scottie to go out there, be comfortable, have fun and be the Scottie Scheffler he is every week.

"I don't want him to take a burden on. He's not going to win or lose us this Presidents Cup. The Presidents Cup is won or lost by 12 people."

Ogilvy, the 2006 US Open champion, helped in a redesign of Medinah, which reopened in 2024 and could play soft this week due to rain.

"From an architecture standpoint, I would love to see it play firm. We built it to play firm," he said.

"To see some things played out exactly as we thought, and then other things it has... just been fun to watch them play it."

South Korean Kim Si-woo is the top-ranked Internationals golfer at 13th followed by New Zealand rookie Ryan Fox at 24th.

Other veterans include Japan's Hideki Matsuyama, South Korean Tom Kim and Australians Min Woo Lee and Adam Scott, who makes his 12th Presidents Cup start still seeking his first victory.

Ogilvy's captain's choices included three rookies -- Japan's Ryo Hisatsune, Canada's Nick Taylor and Colombian Nico Echavarria -- plus Canada's Corey Conners, South Korean Im Sung-jae and South African Christiaan Bezuidenhout.

"The spirit of this group is really strong. I think we're more together than we've ever been," Ogilvy said. "I think the time is right. The boys know we're close. They want to win this."

articles.body:
The New York Jets recently suffered their first loss of the season with a tough overtime defeat at the hands of the Green Bay Packers at home. Making matters worse was the fact that defensive end David Bailey appeared to suffer an injury during the contest, causing some fans to wonder about his status moving forward.

Thankfully, on Wednesday, the team got a positive update on that front.

"David Bailey has an elbow injury but Glenn said he's fine," reported Brian Costello of the New York Post on X, formerly Twitter.

However, it wasn't all good news on the injury front for the Jets on Wednesday.

"DT David Onyemata had core-muscle surgery. Expected to be back by the end of the year, per Glenn," reported Rich Cimini of ESPN on X.

It's unclear exactly how long Onyemata's recovery process is expected to take, but clearly, he isn't anticipated to be back anytime soon.

In his absence, it will be up to Bailey and the other members of the Jets' restructured defensive line, which lost Quinnen Williams via trade last season, to pick up the slack.

Overall, the Jets have been more competitive than many expected so far this year, knocking off the Tennessee Titans in blowout fashion in Week 1 on the road before giving the Packers all they could handle on Sunday afternoon.

Thus far, Aaron Glenn seems to have the team playing inspired football, even as his clock management woes of last year have clearly not improved in 2026.

articles.title: Tramon Williams’ pick-6 among great Packers performances against Falcons
articles.summary: You never pass up an excuse to talk about Tramon Williams burning Atlanta.
articles.body:
The Packers and Falcons will meet for the 37th time in the regular season tomorrow night. While not exactly a storied rivalry, these two teams have certainly had a few interesting matchups, and they've produced a few great performances for the Packers as well.

Here are the highlights, including one game from all the way back in 1970.

Passing yards – 396 ( Aaron Rodgers, 2011 )

En route to his first MVP, Aaron Rodgers sliced and diced the Atlanta Falcons ' secondary in 2011, following up his one-man destruction of the Georgia Dome in the playoffs the previous year. His 396 yards included 140 just to James Jones , who went 70 yards for a touchdown in the third quarter to give the Packers' the lead for the first time in what would become a 25-14 win.

Rushing yards – 155 ( Ahman Green, 2002 )

In some grim foreshadowing, the Packers had trouble with Michael Vick at Lambeau Field to open up the 2002 season . The Falcons, however, had even more trouble with Ahman Green, who carried 27 times for 155 yards to help the Packers to a 37-34 overtime victory. Green also added 42 yards on six catches.

Samkon Gado gets an honorable mention here, too. He rushed for 103 yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta in 2005 , but we'll have more from him later on.

A second honorable mention goes to Donny Anderson, the only player in Packers history to surpass the 100-yard mark against the Falcons twice: once in 1968 and once in 1969 .

Receiving yards – 186 ( Carroll Dale, 1970 )

I'd have guessed the top yardage game would have come from either James Jones in the aforementioned 2011 game or from Jordy Nelson circa 2014, but Carroll Dale had both of them beat before Jones or Nelson was even born.

In 1970, Dale caught four passes for 186 yards and two touchdowns, including an 89-yard strike from Don Horn that put the Packers ahead for good. Horn's pass traveled an impressive 56 yards in the air, which would have been the longest completion by air yards in the NFL in 2025.

I told you we'd mention Samkon Gado again. Well, here we are.

Dr. Gado is one of two Packers to score three touchdowns in a game against the Falcons, doing so in the aforementioned 2005 game. In that game, he rushed for two touchdowns and added a third through the air to cap off a four catch, five yard, one touchdown receiving performance.

The other Packers player to hit a touchdown triumvirate against the Falcons is Robert Tonyan . Big Bob put three across against the Falcons in 2020 as a part of a dominant Packers win .

Squaring off against the Falcons at Milwaukee County Stadium, the Packers got a serious boost from Tim Harris via his four sacks. One came on the Falcons' final drive , which helped preserve the Packers' 23-21 victory.

Also noteworthy, Za'Darius Smith recorded three sacks against the Falcons in the Packers' 2020 win at Lambeau Field. Now a member of the Falcons, you have to think Smith has a pretty good shot at hitting that number again, especially if he's working against Anthony Belton .

A week after firing Mike McCarthy, the Packers got their first of two wins in the short-lived Joe Philbin era with a 34-20 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Blake Martinez led the defensive effort, recording 11 solo tackles as the Packers shut down the Falcons.

Counting playoff games, three different players have recorded two interceptions in a game against the Falcons.

Herb Adderley did it first, picking off the Falcons twice in 1968 .

Mark Murphy (no, not that one) did it next, also grabbing two interceptions during a 1988 shutout loss in Atlanta.

And finally, Tramon Williams did it best. His leaping interception late in the second quarter of the Packers' 2010 Divisional Round victory over the Falcons set up what would become the go-ahead drive for the Packers. The Packers scored so quickly that they left time on the clock for the Falcons to try to rally. They tried…and they got burned .

articles.title: Packers Legendary QB Lynn Dickey Blasts Coach Matt LaFleur
articles.summary: Lynn Dickey, who's in the Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame, ripped coach Matt LaFleur for the team's l;ack of discipline.
articles.body:
Quarterback Lynn Dickey is a Green Bay Packers legend.

And Wednesday Dickey went on a legendary rant, calling out Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur.

Appearing on The Bill Michaels Show, Dickey lambasted LaFleur and the Packers for their ridiculous 26 penalties through two games. Not only does Green Bay lead the league in penalties and penalty yards (231), the Packers are on pace to set NFL records in both of those categories.

Green Bay is 1-1 heading into its game with Atlanta Thursday night, and LaFleur has become the frontrunner to be the first coach fired this season.

"I don't know the personality of Matt LaFleur, but it sure appears to be very passive, and like, 'I don't want to get down guys' throats.' But sometimes that's what you've got to do," Dickey said of the Packers' penalty issues. "They make a lot of money. We all know that. But you've got to want to be disciplined and controlled and the way this thing is going right now, boy does it stink. I'd like to say something different about it, but that's what I see."

Dickey, who quarterbacked the Packers from 1976-85, threw for 21,369 yards and 133 touchdowns in that time. In 1983, Dickey powered the Packers to a then-team record 429 points and threw a league-high 32 touchdown passes.

Dickey still ranks second in team history for most passing yards in a season (4,458 in 1983). He also holds the Green Bay record for highest completion percentage in a game with a minimum of 20 attempts (19–21, 90.48%) against New Orleans in 1981.

Dickey played for Bart Starr from 1976-1983, then under Forrest Gregg his final two seasons in Green Bay. While the Packers lacked discipline under Gregg, they were consistently among the NFL's least penalized teams with Starr in charge.

"We didn't have the greatest talent when I played, but almost every year we were in the top-three of fewest penalties," said Dickey, who's a member of the Packers' Hall of Fame. "And why?

"Bart Starr went over and over and over and demanded that all the time. And I see the stupid penalties post-play, unsportsmanlike stuff. You know, that's all coaching. And just right now man, it is a bomb. And something better change."

At this point, Dickey certainly isn't optimistic that will happen.

"(They're) the most undisciplined team," Dickey said during the radio show. "Penalties are coaching and if you don't get after people and demand that they do the correct things, that's coaching."

The Presidents Cup begins Thursday, Sept. 24, when the United States and the International squads go head-to-head at Medinah Country Club Course No. 3.

U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker leads the Stars and Stripes as they take on Geoff Ogilvy's roster that boasts a trio of major winners in Adam Scott, Hideki Matsuyama and Ryan Fox.

The U.S. leads the one-sided, biennial affair , 13-1-1. The lone International Team victory came in 1998 in Australia.

Golf Channel and Golf Channel mobile will provide live, on-site coverage all week from Medinah to keep fans in the know on everything happening inside and outside of the ropes.

During Wednesday's live show, Snedeker and Ogilvy will reveal their pairings for the first fourball matches. That is scheduled to take place at 4:45 p.m. ET.

Here's a look at how you can stay locked in all of the news and action from the 16th edition of the Presidents Cup :

Noon-12:30PM: Presidents Cup, Opening Ceremony (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

12:30-7PM: Presidents Cup, Day 1 fourballs (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

7-9PM: Live From the Presidents Cup (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

2-7PM: Presidents Cup, Day 2 foursomes (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

8-9AM: Presidents Cup, Day 3 fourballs (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

9AM-7PM: Presidents Cup, Day 3 fourballs and foursomes (NBC/Peacock)

Noon-6PM: Presidents Cup, final-day singles (NBC/Peacock)

6-8PM: Live From the Presidents Cup (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

The first session features five fourball matches, the first of which tees off at 12:35 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kansas State Football: Depth Chart Review vs Tulane- Defense
articles.summary: After a slow start, the Wildcat defense took control, but questions about the run defense linger.
articles.body:
Wendell Gregory : Snaps – 50 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 3 – Sacks – .5

Darien Whitaker Jr. : Snaps – 43 – Tackles – 3 – T.F.L. – 1.5 – Sacks – 1.5

Jayden Bryant: Snaps – 29 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 2 – Sacks – 2

Elijah Hill : Snaps – 11 – Tackles – 1 – T.F.L. – 1 – Sacks – 1

I split the defensive ends and interior defensive linemen because one group dominated the game while the other struggled. The Defensive ends contributed 7.5 tackles for loss and 5 sacks. That's domination. Gregory and Whitaker look like an elite defensive end pairing, with Bryant and Hill providing quality depth. The Wildcats are 3rd in the nation in tackles for loss. I'm pretty sure they're around the top in sacks as well, but the NCAA's stats website is refusing to give up the data.

Gregory and Whitaker Jr. are the clear headliners, but don't sleep on Jayden Bryant. He brought some extra juice to the pass rush as well. Tulane struggled to find him when he was on the field.

This group is playing like one of the nation's best defensive end groups and, in fact, might be one of the best defensive end groups in the nation.

Kamari Burns: Snaps – 34 – Tackles – 2 – T.F.L. – .5

If you're looking for something to worry about, I've got you. The interior defensive line struggled mightily in this one. Travis Bates looked like a defensive end playing defensive tackle while struggling to get off blocks in the run game. PFF credited him with 2 QB hurries, which is great for a defensive tackle, but he also missed 2 tackles, which isn't so great. 52 snaps with no recordable stats isn't a great outing.

Kamari Burns wasn't much better. He was credited with 2 stops, but like Bates, he also had 2 missed tackles. Burns did a better job of holding his ground, but Tulane was able to find some space in the A and B gaps. Eli Jackson did some good things in his 21 snaps, but man, Burns has to stay healthy because a Jackson and Bates pairing would be an open invitation to run inside.

If I were an opposing offensive coordinator, my entire focus would be finding ways to exploit K-State's undersized and thin (in terms of depth) interior line. Tulane's offensive line got some real push up the middle, and their backs were able to hit holes at full speed, making tackling at the second level difficult for the linebackers and safeties.

The coaching staff will have to work around this issue all season. They really need another run-stuffing defensive tackle to emerge. The Wildcats may be the only P4 team in the nation where 2 of the top 3 defensive tackles on the roster are significantly under 300 pounds.

Gabe Powers: Snaps – 61 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 1.5 – Sacks – 0 – Force Fumbles – 1

Mekhi Mason: Snaps – 43 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 1 – Sacks – 1

Rex Van Wyhe: Snaps – 22 – Tackles – 5 – T.F.L. – 1 – Sacks – 0

Speaking of undersized, Mason and Powers are fine individually, but as a pair, they play better running sideline to sideline than getting downhill and taking on running backs in the hole. Ideally, one of them would carry a little more weight in their rear end to hold up against a power running attack. Powers got dinged for 2 missed tackles, and while Mason didn't miss any tackles, it felt like he wasn't in position to make as many as he should have in the run game.

Thankfully, Rex Van Wyhe has emerged as a functional running-stuffing option at linebacker. He made the most of his 22 snaps and, at 245 pounds, is better suited to take on offensive linemen head-on. Van Wyhe played the best game of his Kansas State career against Tulane and could see more action moving forward, especially against run-oriented teams.

Depth is also a major concern at this spot.

Kaleb Patterson: Snaps – 62 – Tackles – 2 – Pass Break-Ups – 1

JoJo Scott: Snaps – 55 – Tackles – 2 – Pass Break-Ups – 1

Rich was targeted 3 times and gave up 3 receptions. That seems bad until you realize those 3 receptions totaled 20 yards, with a long of 12. Tulane decided not to challenge CB1, which was a smart decision.

Since the ball wasn't heading Zashon's way, Kaleb Patterson and JoJo Scott saw plenty of action. Patterson was targeted 5 times and gave up 2 receptions. Unfortunately, those two receptions totaled 41 yards. JoJo Scott was targeted 6 times and gave up 2 receptions. Unfortunately, those two receptions totaled 52 yards, including a 41-yarder.

The thing about playing with a legit lockdown corner like Rich is that the ball tends to head your way more often than usual. Patterson and Scott are going to be tested by every team on Kansas State's schedule. Rich, Patterson, and Scott pretty much went the distance on Saturday. Tulane's offense didn't require more than 3 corners on the field.

The coaching staff brought in Ben Osueke, who started 12 games for Temple last season and was on the All-AAC 3rd team in 2025, last week. I'll be interested to see if he makes it onto the field against Cincinnati.

Wesley Fair: Snaps – 51 – Tackles – 8 – T.F.L. – .5

Logan Bartley : Snaps – 16 – Tackles – 3

Beasley is an interesting case. He was a 4-star, top-150 recruit and was considered the 6th-best player in Ohio coming out of high school. He signed with Ryan Walters and Purdue , witnessed the football equivalent of the Hindenburg as a freshman, and hit the eject button. After a year of football rehab at Miami, Ohio, he's starting for Kansas State. This dude was one of the fastest players in the class of 2024, and he sort of fell into Kansas State's lap, almost as an afterthought. Now you're starting to see what all of the recruiting fuss was about. His speed is a difference-maker in the back end. He can outrun 99% of receivers. Seriously, no one is throwing the ball over his head. He's not very big and is going to miss some tackles in run support (he missed 2 against Tulane), but that's why guys like Logan Bartley are on the roster. To steal from the running backs, Beasley is the lighting and Bartley is the thunder.

Unfortunately, the thunder went down with an injury early, but most teams can't bring their 2025 starter off the bench if their 2026 starter gets hurt. Fair's 8 tackles led the Wildcats, and he was also credited with a team-high 3 "stops" by PFF, while only missing one tackle. Tulane targeted him once in the passing game and completed a 6-yard pass. I thought Bartley going down was going to be a big blow to the defense, but Fair stepped in and didn't miss a beat.

Beasley kept a lid on the defense from his free safety position, and Fair terrorized the Green Wave around the line of scrimmage. After last season, the safety position felt all but safe, but it may be one of the deepest and most talented position groups on the roster with the addition of Beasley, the emergence of Bartley, and the dependability of Fair. That's not even taking into consideration All-ACC honorable mention safety Ja'son Prevard and Georgia transfer Adrian Maddox, who at one point were considered potential starters for the Wildcats.

It's truly an embarrassment of riches on the back end of the defense.

articles.title: Mets' Nolan McLean puts finishing touches on excellent rookie campaign: 'Proud of him'
articles.summary: Mets right-hander Nolan McLean ended his rookie campaign by going 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA, eighth-lowest in the NL, in 31 starts.
articles.body:
Before Wednesday's game between the Mets and Texas Rangers , manager Andy Green was asked what is the biggest area in Nolan McLean 's game that he can take a step forward in to reach that next level that the skipper always talks about.

Green mentioned the right-hander throwing strikes consistently and limiting his walks, but was quick to say, "and that's not by diminishing stuff, it's by using the stuff you have and understanding how to get ahead and to finish."

It was one of the many times this season that Green spoke about his young players in a way that seemed to challenge them – even when they've played great – because he knows they're capable of more.

Shortly thereafter, McLean took the mound and, heeding his manager's advice, looked amazing through four perfect innings. Things went awry for the rookie in the fifth inning, however, when the Rangers tagged him for two runs after McLean allowed three hits and a walk in the inning.

Just a few hours before that, Green practically predicted it.

"I actually think he does that really well for a pretty good portion of each game and then there's usually one inning where it's like here for a little, kinda lost it, now I found it again, now I compete, now I get out of it," the skipper said. "The less and less he does that, and look he's not gonna be perfect, but the more he drives that down and the less and less he does that he's gonna get himself out of more jams by not getting into them."

The foreshadowing by Green was uncanny, though it shouldn't come as a surprise considering he's known most of these young players since they joined the organization as the Senior Vice President for Player Development.

After that difficult fifth inning, McLean went right back to being dominant and retired the next six batters in order on just 13 pitches to complete his final outing of the season. Even in the fifth inning, the right-hander had the bases loaded with one out and managed to exit with just one run scoring.

"Those guys were aggressive so any time a team's aggressive like that and you're filling up the strike zone, you're relying a lot on your defense and sometimes they just don't hit it at guys and in the fifth inning they hit a few balls away from people and that's part of it," McLean said. "So I was just kind of trusting my stuff that they were eventually gonna hit it at people to try to minimize and if I get to two strikes I'll execute a pitch and punch him out.

"And then going back out in the sixth, making sure to keep that same game plan and not necessarily getting tentative just because they put a few balls in play [earlier]."

McLean ended his rookie campaign by going 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA, eighth-lowest in the NL, in 31 starts. He's also the only Mets starter this season who didn't miss a single start, impressive for a 25-year-old rookie whose season started at the World Baseball Classic pitching for Team USA.

"I try to take pride in going out there and competing every single time, whether I have my stuff or not and that's what matters most to me, just going out there and making each start," McLean said.

Meanwhile, Green, for all his challenges that he gives his players, was impressed with McLean's body of work and knows the right-hander will get back to work soon enough after he enjoys this one just a little while longer.

"I don't think that was like his vintage stuff and it still found a way to be really, really good," Green said about McLean's outing on Wednesday. "Velocity was a little bit down today. Last outing of a long season that started at the WBC and felt that he competed incredibly well today.

"He's just kind of the person he's been, just figure out a way to get it done even if it doesn't feel your best. So [I'm] proud of him, proud of the season he's had. He's got a lot to hang his hat on right now and I know it won't take long for him to get back to work and get going."

As for whether or not McLean did enough to take home the NL Rookie of the Year honors in what has become a solid class that includes teammate Carson Benge , Green isn't so sure his right-hander will be in the conversation.

Nevertheless, it doesn't take hardware to know what kind of pitcher McLean is.

"He's the best rookie pitcher in the National League and I think that's pretty obvious to everybody," Green said.

articles.title: Celtics news: Jayson Tatum, Paul George link up for golf outing
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum is getting one last break from the NBA grind before Boston Celtics training camp begins, and he spent it with some of his former teammates. Tat...
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum is getting one last break from the NBA grind before Boston Celtics training camp begins, and he spent it with some of his former teammates .

Tatum was recently spotted playing golf with Paul George and former Celtics teammate Malcolm Brogdon . Photos and videos from the outing made the rounds on social media, showing the three NBA veterans enjoying some downtime before the start of the 2026-27 season.

Celtics' social media account shared the image on X, formerly Twitter

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Squad goes golfing ⛳️," the caption read.

The group brought together former and current players from two Eastern Conference rivals, but there was plenty of history between them. Brogdon spent the 2022-23 season in Boston and won the Sixth Man of the Year award during his lone season with the Celtics. He later moved around the league before joining Philadelphia .

George, meanwhile, has remained one of Tatum's longtime friends . The two have worked out together during past offseasons and have often shown mutual respect for each other's games.

Their friendship has continued despite playing for teams that could see plenty of each other during the regular season. The offseason has also changed the connection between the Celtics and 76ers . Philadelphia added former Boston star Jaylen Brown as part of its roster overhaul.

For Tatum, the golf outing comes after a busy summer for Boston. The Celtics have gone through significant roster changes, leaving Tatum as the team's clear centerpiece heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

Training camp is now close, which means the relaxed days of the offseason are almost over.

articles.title: Holborn and St Pancras: 15 candidates in race to replace Starmer
articles.summary: There are 15 candidates standing in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election on Thursday 8 October.
articles.body:
On 8 October, voters in the Holborn and St Pancras constituency will choose their next MP.

A win in this seat, which has returned Labour MPs for decades, would be a feather in the cap of the Green Party after Sir Keir Starmer stood down from the House of Commons at the start of September, shortly after leaving office as prime minister.

Labour are confident of holding on, but the Greens also have high hopes of winning their first London seat - and there are 13 other candidates in the mix all hoping to take this central London constituency.

BBC London spoke to five of the leading candidates.

Zack Polanski, the Green Party candidate, told BBC London he was "feeling confident or I wouldn't have put my hat in the ring in the first place, but I'm not complacent".

He said he would "work with the Labour government constructively on the things we agree with".

He added: "But where they're letting us down on things like housing, on nationalising Thames Water, on tackling the climate crisis - they're talking about drilling for new oil and gas - voting Green and sending me to Parliament is a way to keep this Labour government in check."

Polanski, who is a member of the London Assembly and leader of the Green Party in England and Wales, said people in the constituency "desperately need change".

"People are telling me over and over again they can't afford the cost of housing, they need more council housing.

"Renters who need rent control, leaseholders who need justice for leaseholders. The government said they'd end this feudal system of leasehold and then haven't taken the action."

When asked about the last time he ran in Camden, as a Liberal Democrat candidate for the council, he said: "I think in politics we need less politicians who treat political parties like football teams.

"Someone picks a team and they have to stick with it for life no matter what they do.

"Actually, there's lots of people including Liberal Democrats in this constituency that will recognise I'm the only person in this constituency who can beat Labour."

Sagal Abdi-Wali, Labour's candidate, said the campaign had been "really good" so far.

She told BBC London: "It's quite a big deal politically, absolutely

"Andy Burnham's first by-election, standing against the Green Party leader; yeah, quite a big test for the party... you have the responsibility to deliver."

Abdi-Wali, whose family came to London from Somalia as refugees in the 1990s when she was a child, has been the leader of Camden Council since May.

She told BBC London: "For me, I'm just so excited.

"We've got an opportunity to make sure that we send a Labour member of Parliament that would be really local and really visible and committed to this area, someone who comes from this area.

"I grew up in this area my whole life. It's made me, Camden made me who I am, and to be able to now represent us in Parliament will be such a major thing."

Abdi-Wali acknowledged there were problems with housing and crime in the constituency.

"I want to make sure that particularly with housing, for instance, it's an issue. It's a crisis here in Camden. It's a crisis in London. It's a crisis all over the country and it needs a national response."

Abdi-Wali praised the former MP, Sir Keir.

"The work that Keir did as the member of Parliament for here for 11 years and before that the 30 years that he gave to social justice.

"Now with Andy Burnham, we have an opportunity to really work on a lot of those issues."

Peter Newman, the Reform UK candidate, said he served in the Metropolitan Police for 31 years from 1978 to 2009.

He told BBC London: "I had a good and varied career, but you know the time has come when, you know, woke leadership was getting too far into the Met."

Newman said he was standing because "I couldn't walk by any more".

"The chaos of the Conservatives and Labour that have left this country in, I had to do something.

"Reform is the only option for the people of Holborn and St Pancras, the only option in fact for the country."

He said the party was "picking up votes all the time in local elections".

"We're improving our percentages in London all the time, and we've got a tough election. And the people of Holborn and St Pancras, they want change.

"They've been let down by Keir Starmer, who clearly used it as a stepping stone just to become prime minister."

He says on the doorstep, voters are telling him "they're fed up with the crime, disorder. This borough is crime-ridden. It's soaked in crime."

If elected, Newman said he would be "relentless in pursuing the police chiefs and the mayor of London and his policing advisers in finding out what's gone wrong with policing in London".

Lib Dem candidate Patrick Stillman said his party's ground game in the by-election was helping it reintroduce itself.

He told BBC London: "We've got a really good liberal message: we care about the things you care about, and we're going to work really hard for you."

Stillman is a Camden councillor, representing West Hampstead in the north of the borough.

The party led a joint Conservative-Lib Dem administration when the council was under no overall control from 2006 to 2010.

He said the by-election "is our opportunity really to sort of re-represent ourselves and say, 'Actually, you know, look at the great work our team are doing, look at the great things we're saying in Parliament - wouldn't you like a bit of that here?'"

Stillman added: "We find community champions, we get leaflets through doors, we talk to people on their doorstep about what matters to them.

"That revolves around a lot of good activists, and sometimes it's a case of if you don't do something in an area for a while those people fade away and move away and then you find yourself a bit more boxed in.

"For us that's what I'm really excited about. With Holborn and St Pancras is a chance to get back on the doors, to get back into communities, to get back picking up issues of local people and saying, 'We'll champion them for you.'"

Ewan Cameron, the Conservative candidate, said he was the only candidate in the by-election talking about the housing crisis.

He told BBC London: "My opponents, what are they doing? They're talking about segregation. They're on the ballot paper, they want to have religion. Religion's not what we should be discussing.

"We should be in a position where every day, whether you're Jewish, whether you're Muslim, whether you have no faith, we all have the same issues. And again and again those issues are, what?

"Holborn and St Pancras is no longer family-friendly, there's not enough family homes."

Cameron, who was a Camden councillor for the Belsize ward from 1998 to 2002 and sat on the council's development control committee, said crime was another priority in his campaign.

"If you come out of work at night and walk home and you don't feel safe, who do you blame? I blame Labour. Labour has been the local MP, they have control of the local council, you've got Sadiq Khan who's the local Labour mayor; again and again London's not safe.

"The fact that the police sometimes come, but not always. But the blatant, the blatantness of the theft, it leaves you speechless."

Cameron added: "Camden [Council] sits on its hands and my biggest concern is the fact that if Labour win Holborn and St Pancras, they'll just be complacent."

The Holborn and St Pancras by-election will be held on Thursday 8 October.

articles.title: Why are data centres in East of England being branded 'insane'?
articles.summary: A group says the annual emissions of two proposed data centres will be greater than Luton Airport.
articles.body:
As the UK's dash for data centres shows no sign of slowing down, two councillors have highlighted a new concern over the facilities – on-site gas production.

Proposals for two hyperscale data centres in Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire have been branded "insane" by Ed Gemmell, a councillor for Buckinghamshire Council, as they include gas power stations.

The government has designated data centres as "critical infrastructure" and said claims they were "draining the country's water or blowing carbon targets" were false.

"I'm not AI [artificial intelligence] averse, but saying we can't get enough electricity so we need a gas power station is a really terrible idea," said Susan Clinch, a Central Bedfordshire councillor.

"The International Energy Agency notes that the carbon savings enabled by AI could be three to four times larger than the emissions created by the data centres themselves," a government spokesperson said.

Quest Park has proposed building a data centre at Quest Pit, a former quarry it owns next to the planned Universal theme park in Bedfordshire.

The company said the £9.5bn project would provide more than 1,000 jobs.

SDC Capital Partners is proposing to build another data centre at a former landfill site next to the M40 in Buckinghamshire, between Gerrards Cross and Beaconsfield.

The area sits within the largest cluster of data centres in the UK, known as the Slough Availability Zone, and SDC said the facility could provide 400 jobs.

The second public consultation into SDC's plans is currently under way.

Blake Stephenson, the Conservative MP for Mid Bedfordshire, who also sits on the Environmental Audit Committee, said he felt Quest Park was the wrong site for a "huge data centre", but acknowledged it was important to have UK facilities for "national security and personal data protection".

"They're really critical to our economy and they're really critical to the services that we all rely on," he said.

Data centres require a large amount of power to run and existing facilities consume about 2.5% of the UK's electricity.

The UK's daily energy demand, on average, is 30GW, according to the National Energy System Operator (NESO).

It added the UK generates between 25GW and 33GW of electricity on an average day, via technologies, including wind, solar, nuclear and gas.

Quest Park would have a power load - the total amount of electrical power drawn at any given time - of 1GW and SDC's site would require 300MW.

About 1GW of electricity could power three million average British homes, according to NESO.

Quest Park and SDC's proposals said on-site gas would provide "resilience" and prevent heavy demand on the National Grid.

Both companies said they plan to connect to the grid once it can meet the demand of their sites.

Foxglove, a campaign group, estimated the combined greenhouse gas emissions of both plants - if operating at full capacity and powered by gas - could be as high as 4.5m tonnes per year.

The figure is three times as much as Luton Airport's emissions, which were 1.3m tonnes in 2025 .

The Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit, a not-for-profit organisation that looks at the impacts of climate change, agreed with Foxglove's calculations, adding typically two units of gas were required to produce one unit of electricity.

"I'm flabbergasted, it's insane," said Buckinghamshire independent councillor Ed Gemmell, who also leads the Climate Party.

"We are not against data centres as long as they come with their own independent energy source – but we assumed that would be renewables.

"Ideally they should be built near the coast to incorporate tidal power, which is totally reliable," said Gemmell.

David Kohler, the director of Quest Park, told the BBC the company's energy mix was still a "work in progress" and that incorporating renewable power was "sensible" but had to be "feasible".

He said creating 1GW of solar electricity would require an area equivalent to 15% of Bedfordshire, and that wind power was "intermittent and expensive".

He said the company was considering alternative technologies that did not rely on gas combustion.

"Foxglove's 'worst case' calculations [for] Quest Park are unduly pessimistic," Kohler added.

SDC's original proposal to the government included an "integrated gas turbine energy generation centre".

Its consultation documents also put forward a second option of an electrical sub-station.

An SDC spokesperson said: "It is premature to be speculating on CO2 emissions as we are still working to determine what energy solutions are most appropriate for the campus.

"Once this work is completed, we look forward to presenting our finalised power strategy."

A change in planning regulations means data centres can be approved by the government instead of local councils.

Both SDC and Quest Park submitted documents asking to be considered as "nationally significant infrastructure projects (NSIP)", which the government agreed to do.

This allows them to apply directly to the Planning Inspectorate for permission for the projects, - which has not yet happened.

Rebecca Hare, independent councillor for Houghton Conquest on Central Bedfordshire Council, said: "The biggest concern from local people is the way these NSIP applications happen. The community feels blindsided."

She said: "There are obviously benefits [to data centres]: faster internet, cloud-based working, working from home, but we're bearing the brunt of a lot of national infrastructure in this area."

Hare added: "It feels like national strategy doesn't make sense – with these gas works required to fuel it, when we're working towards net zero."

Clinch, a Green Party councillor, said many local people were "hugely concerned" over the data centres but "feel there's nothing they can do" due to the planning process.

She backed calls by the Green Party for the government to "pause" approval of data centres until a more stringent environmental framework was in place.

A government spokesperson responded: "Not building new data centres would simply send investment and good jobs abroad, while leaving Britain dependent on other countries for processing sensitive health and defence data.

"This does not mean a blank cheque for big tech, or that every data centre should be approved.

"Developers should prioritise clean power, use water responsibly, create British jobs and supply chains, and provide investment to the communities in which they are built."

Stephenson said while the Conservative Party was "not anti-gas turbine", his preference for data centres was "that we always build on brownfield [land] first, and connect into the grid without gas turbines".

He added that during an Environmental Audit Committee session in July, he questioned a technology company about how much brownfield land was available across the country "with ready access to the grid, such that data centres with gas turbines shouldn't be needed".

He said there should be a "halfway house" when it came to planning decisions.

"It's important that government focuses on getting critical infrastructure built, because we need that for the future of our economy and prosperity, but we can't ignore local people at the same time," he added.

articles.title: Wolverhampton airport owner killed in Swiss Alps plane crash
articles.summary: Tony Hall, Wolverhampton Halfpenny Green Airport owner, has died alongside two others in the crash.
articles.body:
An airport owner, businessman and "incredible dad" from the West Midlands has been named as one of three people killed in a plane crash in the Swiss Alps last week.

Anthony Hall, known as Tony, owned Wolverhampton Halfpenny Green Airport in Staffordshire and was the managing director of Pegasus, a construction and recycling company based in Lye, near Stourbridge.

In a statement, his family said they were "completely heartbroken by the loss of a truly wonderful husband, devoted father and much-loved man".

They added: "Tony was an exceptional businessman who achieved great things in the construction/haulage industry, and his commitment to succeed and progress never faltered.

"He was first and foremost a loving husband and an incredible dad to his daughter, whose family meant everything to him.

"We will miss him immensely and will remember him as the kind, caring, generous, determined and fantastic character he was."

Authorities said the plane took off from Sion airport in the Rhône Valley and, for unknown reasons, crashed into a mountain slope about 10 minutes later.

Emergency teams from the Valais Rescue Organisation, police and firefighters were sent to the scene along with three helicopters.

Owain Davies, a 55-year-old businessman from west Wales, has been identified as a second Briton killed in the crash.

The Swiss Transportation Safety Board has begun an investigation.

Hall's family added they were incredibly grateful for the kindness, love, and support that had been shown to them since his death.

"Our hearts go out to those who also lost their lives in this terrible tragedy," they said, and asked for privacy as they came to terms with their loss.

Former Stourbridge MP Suzanne Webb paid tribute to Hall, a friend, on Thursday, saying he was "one of the very best".

"Tony will always be a legend to me. What he achieved in helping build Pegasus into the success it is today, alongside the other directors, was remarkable," she said.

"But beyond the business, Tony was great fun to be around and, quite simply, a genuinely good person. I will miss his quick wit and humour."

Webb added he gave "so much" to the area, particularly through his support for the Poppy Appeal and Military Vehicle Parade.

"Having served in the armed forces, he gave his support willingly," she said.

"His life was tragically cut short, but what he achieved after leaving the army was truly inspiring, and he did it with a passion I was always in awe of."

Wolverhampton Halfpenny Green Airport also issued a tribute to its owner and director, who bought the site in 2023.

He had a "clear vision" for it to become "the best general aviation airport in the country", the statement said, and "poured his time, energy and passion" into securing its future.

"Together with his co-owner, he transformed the airport, creating a thriving aviation hub for the local and wider aviation community," it added.

"His passion, determination and commitment have left a lasting mark on the airport and on the many people who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him."

In another statement, a Pegasus spokesperson spoke about their "immense sadness" over Hall's death.

"He built a strong team and a business with values and solid foundations, which he was incredibly proud of," they said.

Pegasus would continue to operate as usual, "just as Tony would have wanted", the company added.

"Above everything else, Tony was a much-loved husband, father, friend, and colleague. He will be deeply missed."

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office previously confirmed it was "providing support to the families of two British nationals who died in Switzerland".

It added officials were in contact with the local authorities and its thoughts were with the families of those who had died.

articles.title: Manu Elvira, un golfista al alza: “Gente desconocida me escribió para decirme que ya eran fans míos”
articles.standfirst: Aunque no ganó el domingo pasado en Wentworth, el cántabro Manu Elvira enamoró, emocionó y se demostró a sí mismo que puede competir con los mejores
articles.summary: Aunque no ganó el domingo pasado en Wentworth, el cántabro Manu Elvira enamoró, emocionó y se demostró a sí mismo que puede competir con los mejores
articles.body: Manuel Elvira (Santander, 30 años) quedó segundo el pasado domingo en el BMW PGA Championship, el torneo más destacado del DP World Tour. Compitió de tú a tú con varios de los mejores jugadores del mundo y nos emocionó con un eagle en el hoyo 17 que casi le otorga el triunfo. Por desgracia, cerró el torneo con un doble bogey, pero sin duda él se queda con lo positivo. Hoy comienza a jugar el Open de Francia. Pregunta. ¿Ha digerido ya todo lo que pasó la semana pasada? Respuesta. Sí. El lunes no lo había digerido todavía y me golpeó un poco todo. El martes vino un poco de bajón físico-emocional, pero ya está todo digerido y estoy con ganas de empezar este Open de Francia, a ver si somos capaces de hacerlo igual de bien o mejor. P. ¿Qué espera de este torneo, después de una semana como la anterior? R. Si algo he aprendido en estos años que llevo en el Tour es a no tener muchas expectativas, porque creo que luego te pueden rebotar. Sé que jugué muy bien la semana pasada y quiero mantener ese ritmo, pero tampoco sin meterme una presión extra porque lo haya hecho muy bien en el anterior torneo. Estoy con ganas de hacerlo bien y sé que el juego está en un sitio correcto, pero tampoco quiero ir con esa presión añadida. P. De ese hoyo final en Wentworth, ¿qué se aprende? R. Más que quedarme con lo negativo de lo que pasó en el último hoyo del torneo, me quedo con los otros 71 que jugué y sobre todo con el eagle que hice en el hoyo anterior, en el 17, para ponerme líder. Luego, si es verdad que tuve una estrategia, fallé el golpe de colocación, pero si lo tuviese que volver a hacer lo haría otra vez porque los golpes de 100 metros para abajo es lo que mejor estaba haciendo esa semana, y confiaba que con un tercer golpe a green podía dejarla muy cerca y asegurar el 5. Pero en el golf nunca sabes cuándo vas a fallar un golpe y lo fallé en el momento equivocado. P. No obstante, fue una semana casi para enmarcar. ¿Con qué se queda? R. Como torneo era muy bueno, posiblemente el torneo insignia del European Tour, casi como si fuese un Major de del golf, en un en un campo icónico y viniendo el año pasado de fallar el corte y no jugué muy bien. Con lo que me quedo sobre todo es con el ambiente que hay allí, la cantidad de afición que hay, cómo el público se vuelca con todo el mundo. Y luego me demostré que si juego bien puedo competir de tú a tú con jugadores buenos y estar ahí peleando codo con codo con ellos. Me quedo con que no hay que minusvalorarse a uno mismo y hay verse capaz de hacer ciertas cosas. P. Lo más difícil en el golf es ser consistente. ¿Está más cerca de ese equilibrio? R. No hay que pasarse con las expectativas. Uno no debe creerse el rey del mambo porque de repente has quedado segundo en un torneo muy grande, pero tampoco creerse el peor por quedar el último. A la vez, hay que estar centrado en hacer las cosas que uno puede controlar, ya sea tus rutinas antes de cada golpe o cómo preparas los campos o cómo te preparas las vueltas de entrenamiento. Tampoco hay que obsesionarse con dónde acaba tu bola muchas veces. Si das el cien por cien en todo lo que tú puedes controlar y no dejas que te afecte en exceso lo que no puedes controlar, creo puedes sacar el mayor potencial de tu juego cada semana. P. ¿Cómo valoraría su temporada hasta ahora? R. Tras la semana que vengo de hacer, creo se ha convertido en un sobresaliente. Llevaba jugando bien unas cuantas semanas, aunque no acababan de salir excesivamente bien los resultados. Una semana le pegas muy bien al drive y no acabas pateando tan bien, otra pateas muy bien, pero tampoco le estás pegando muy bien desde el tee o no dejas la bola cerca. Venía haciendo las cosas bien y era cuestión de que una semana cuadrase un todo, y la semana pasada se reflejó eso. Le pegué bien desde el tee, los tiros a green fueron impresionantes todos los días y la verdad con el putt metí bastantes de los importantes y esa es la clave para tener un gran torneo. P. ¿Se puede saber qué le dijo su hermano -Nacho, también golfista- cuando terminó el hoyo 18? R. Sí, me dijo que tenía que estar muy orgulloso, que el eagle que había hecho en el 17 había sido una cosa espectacular y que estuviera orgulloso. Me habló desde la emoción del momento. Es mi hermano y sufrió posiblemente como yo o incluso más viéndolo desde fuera, porque no puedes controlar nada de lo que está pasando, pero no me dijo en ningún momento nada negativo, sino todo lo contrario. Me dijo que había hecho una semana increíble y me recalcó que lo del eagle del 17 y el corazón y la garra que le había echado. P. ¿Es consciente de que hubo mucha gente siguiendo este final de torneo? R. Sí, la verdad que es una cosa de locos, porque al acabar, independientemente del resultado con esa rotura de corazón, por así decirlo, me llegó una cantidad de mensajes de muchísima gente, tanto conocidos como desconocidos, mandándome ánimos. Algunos me decían: ‘te has ganado un nuevo seguidor’. Y oye, esas cosas te alegran mucho independientemente de lo agridulce que fuera el final. P. ¿Se podría decir que el BMW PGA Championship ha situado a Manu Elvira en el mapa de los grandes golfistas? R. A mí me gusta pensar que sí. Estuve en situación de ganar el domingo junto a nombres como Rory [McIlroy], J.J. Spaun, Aaron Ray o Adam Scott, que son ganadores de Majors. Lo pienso, y digo: ‘vaya, es increíble con los nombres con los que has empatado e incluso estuviste liderando durante un tiempo’. Para mí es algo espectacular y no me lo va a quitar nadie. P. Todo eso tiene que dar confianza, imagino. R. Sí, aunque más que confianza, te hace pensar que eres capaz y que si juegas bien puedes pelear con toda esa gente. Eso sí, tampoco me hace pensar que soy mejor que uno o que otro. Te confirma que si juegas una semana bien puedes competir con cualquiera y te ayuda a creértelo, porque a veces hay algunas dudas en uno mismo. Y si ves que eres capaz de hacerlo una vez, por qué no vas a poder hacerlo más veces. P. ¿Cómo se explica que la semana pasada jugar tan bien justo contra los mejores? R. El golf es un poco inexplicable muchas veces, pero es porque venía haciendo las cosas bien, entrenando bien con mi equipo, ya sea temas técnicos de golf, el tema mental o el físico. Fue una cuestión de que la semana cuadrase. Pero la clave yo creo que fue un poco también que entraron los putts, que es lo que al fin y al cabo te ayuda a estar más arriba en los torneos. P. ¿Ve mucho margen de mejora en su juego? R. Algo se puede mejorar siempre. Cosas como ser un poco más certero desde el tee, los tiros a green, el putt siempre se puede mejorar aunque va a rachas. También se puede mejorar un poco el control de velocidades para tripatear los menos posible. P. ¿Qué objetivos tiene a corto plazo? R. Este año, viendo que he sacado buenos puntos y me he puesto en una buena posición, ¿por qué no acabar fuerte la temporada e intentar sacar una de esas tarjetas de del PGA Tour para el año que viene? Creo que las finales de Abu Dhabi y Dubai me las he asegurado, al menos la primera. Sería un sueño ganar una de esas tarjetas. P. ¿Qué sueños tiene a nivel de golf? R. Jugar Majors siempre ha sido un sueño y ahora que he pegado una buena subida en el ranking mundial, si acabo fuerte la temporada, puede estar más cerca de cara al año que viene. Y si acabo esta temporada en el top 20 o top 25 de la Race to Dubai me clasificaría para el British Open del año que viene y es un objetivo bastante accesible. Un sueño más a largo plazo sería disputar la Ryder Cup del 2031 en España. Sería increíble y si la puedo jugar con mi hermano, pues incluso más todavía. P. Su hermano tiene más a tiro esa tarjeta del PGA. R. Sí, lleva un año muy bueno. Empezó ganando en Dubai y luego ha hecho otra serie de torneos muy buenos. P. De Wentworth salió también con un buen cheque. ¿De qué manera ayuda esto a su golf? R. Te ayuda a ir un poco más tranquilo. Además, como he sacado muchos puntos, puedo haberme asegurado las finales y eso es un plus para ir más tranquilo. P. ¿Cuenta con buenos patrocinadores? P. He tenido mucha suerte con las personas y marcas que me han acompañado durante estos años. Algunas han estado conmigo en etapas anteriores y otras siguen a mi lado hoy. Actualmente cuento con Titleist, Lacoste, KPMG, Kyocera, Dejavu y 226ERS, y les estoy muy agradecido por la confianza que han depositado en mí. Al final, detrás de cada marca hay personas con las que compartes experiencias y momentos, y eso hace que la relación vaya mucho más allá de un patrocinio. P. Tiene que ser de gran ayuda contar con un hermano en el circuito. R. Desde luego, porque desde que llegué al circuito ha sido de las mayores ayudas que he tenido, sino la mayor. Para el tema de orientarme, ayudarme con todo, ya sea el tema de hoteles, los campos, entrenar juntos… Nos apoyarnos mutuamente y para mí ha sido un apoyo increíble. P. Para usted es importante trabajar el tema físico y mental. R. Sí, desde luego, he hecho hincapié los últimos meses en el tema mental, ya sea para afrontar los errores cuando las vueltas no están yendo bien o cuando la mente se va a algún otro lado y hay que volver al tema presente. Y el tema físico para mí es algo fundamental a la hora de recuperar, porque son muchos viajes a lo largo del año, muchas semanas fuera y al cuerpo eso le pasa factura. Una buena forma física es una gran ayuda. P. No estaría mal inaugurar su palmarés de torneos esta semana, y si no en el Open de España. R. Hombre, todos soñamos con ganar el Open de nuestro país. Ya lo viví con Angelito Hidalgo hace un par de años y para mí fue una inspiración de cara a querer ganarlo yo también, porque con él he compartido muchos años de carrera amateur en equipos nacionales. Yo también quiero conseguirlo y sería un sueño hecho realidad. P. ¿Cómo ayudó a su golf sus años en la Universidad de Florida? R. A nivel de golf a mí me ayudó muchísimo. Tuve la suerte que mi coach allí en Estados Unidos era bastante friki de golf, porque a veces tu coach puede ser más un tutor que te supervisa. Pero mi coach manejaba mucho el tema técnico y sabía mucho y a mí me ayudó bastante a mejorar durante esos cuatro años. Me ayudó mucho con la estrategia en el campo de golf. Luego está también que te enfrentas a muy buenos jugadores de otras universidades y todo esto te prepara para el mundo profesional. Para el aspecto competitivo fue muy importante y a mí me ayudó muchísimo.

articles.title: Team USA golfers welcome Trump’s expected Presidents Cup visit, share pride in representing America
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark and Team USA players react to Trump's expected visit to Medinah for the Presidents Cup, sharing personal stories and patriotism.
articles.body: Wyndham Clark is preparing to represent the United States at the 2026 Presidents Cup, with President Donald Trump expected to watch Sunday’s final round in person. "Being an American, having the President of the United States come and watch you play golf is something, as a kid, you don’t ever imagine or fathom happening," Clark told OutKick on Wednesday. "I just think it’s pretty amazing." The PGA Tour, which organizes the Presidents Cup, invited Trump to serve as honorary chairman, and he accepted. Sources familiar with the president’s plans told OutKick that Trump is expected to attend Sunday’s final round at Medinah Country Club. Like the Ryder Cup, the Presidents Cup is a team match-play competition. It pits 12 U.S. golfers against 12 players from countries outside the U.S. and Europe, while the Ryder Cup matches the Americans against Europe. CANADIANS NICK TAYLOR AND COREY CONNERS LAUGH OFF LAKE ONTARIO RENAMING AHEAD OF PRESIDENTS CUP The competition begins Thursday and runs through Sunday. OutKick spoke with several U.S. players Tuesday and Wednesday about representing their country and Trump’s expected visit. For Sam Burns, the conversation also provided an opportunity to talk about something he would like to see more of at home: Americans pulling for each other. "Being an American, I think it’s very important that we do support our president, regardless of your political views," Burns said. "I think if you look at our country now, it seems more divided than ever, and hopefully we can get back to the point where all Americans come together, and we’re all trying to kind of reach the same goal." Burns said he has played golf with Trump a few times, but emphasized that his respect for the presidency extends beyond whoever happens to hold the job. "Anyone who’s the president of this country, I respect that position, obviously," he said. SAM BURNS IS ONE OF AMERICA'S BEST GOLFERS, BUT FAITH, FAMILY AND THE USA MATTER MORE TO HIM THAN GOLF Chris Gotterup had a similar reaction when asked about the visit. "Whoever the president is, if they care enough to come watch us play golf, that’s pretty cool," Gotterup said. "I know we’re excited, and we’re going to go try to put on a good performance for everyone." Wyndham Clark recalls Trump’s 2023 US Open call For Clark, there is already a memorable Trump interaction to look back on. After winning the 2023 U.S. Open, Clark received a congratulatory call from Trump, who was out of office at the time. Clark described it Wednesday as "one of the coolest calls of my life." His first major victory came at Los Angeles Country Club, where he beat Rory McIlroy by one shot. Apparently, Trump had been paying close attention. "He was so complimentary, just saying how good I played. And honestly, it was amazing. He knew every shot," Clark said. "He was like, ‘This up-and-down on this hole, this up-and-down on this hole was amazing.’ And he really said a bunch of nice things." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Patrick Cantlay’s first meeting with Trump goes back even further. He said they met at the 2011 Walker Cup at Royal Aberdeen and have crossed paths several times since. This week, Cantlay hopes the president’s appearance gives the home crowd something else to get excited about. "I think it’d be great to have the president out, and hopefully it gets the crowd going," Cantlay said. "I’m expecting the crowd to be loud and behind us this week, and that’s what makes playing home team events so fun." Xander Schauffele found a slightly different angle. "I’m sure Secret Service wasn’t pumped that he made an early announcement on where he’s going to be, but they’ll do a nice job to keep him safe," Schauffele joked. "It’s awesome that our president loves golf and supports USA." What representing Team USA means to the players For Jacob Bridgeman, representing the United States at this level is something he has wanted for a long time. "This is the highest honor that you can get in all of golf," Bridgeman said. "Playing for the United States is the best thing that any of us can ever ask for, and it’s an honor." Bridgeman said he hoped to see multiple presidents attend and described the prospect of having them rooting for the Americans as making the experience feel "even more patriotic." US PRESIDENTS CUP PLAYERS EXPLAIN HOW CHRISTIAN FAITH BUILDS FRIENDSHIPS AND PUTS GOLF IN PERSPECTIVE Jackson Koivun, meanwhile, welcomed the chance to have teammates again. "I just love playing for Team USA," he said. "It’s always fun when you’re able to put on the red, white and blue and play on a team with guys who are fighting for the same cause." Love of country is even strong enough to get an Alabama guy and an Auburn guy working together. For a few days, anyway. Justin Thomas, who played college golf at Alabama, offered his practice rounds with former Auburn star Koivun as an example when OutKick asked about sports bringing people together. "I’ve been playing a lot of practice rounds with an Auburn kid this week," Thomas said. "I love him to death, but I hope he has a terrible Saturday," Thomas joked, clarifying that he meant the Saturday after Thanksgiving when Auburn and Alabama face each other in the 2026 Iron Bowl. For now, though, they’re wearing the same colors. "We have everybody here pulling for the USA," Thomas said. Schauffele made a similar point about the opportunity international competition gives Americans to cheer together. "If players and people can kind of gather under one flag in a sport, it is pretty awesome," he said. "Luckily, we’re able to do that in golf." These weeks can fly by during a career, he said, and he expects to appreciate them even more when he looks back. Right now, there is a tournament to win. "All of us guys that are on this squad, there’s nothing more we want to do than to go out and win and represent our country well," Burns said. "And that’s the plan this week."

articles.title: Green Bay Packers receive strong Michael Penix Jr. prediction ahead of Falcons clash
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have plenty to sort out after the first two weeks of the 2026 campaign. The Packers split their opening games and now hold a 1-1 record...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have plenty to sort out after the first two weeks of the 2026 campaign. The Packers split their opening games and now hold a 1-1 record following their overtime victory over the New York Jets . Their next matchup comes on a short turnaround against an Atlanta Falcons team that has struggled early, but another storyline is drawing attention as questions continue to surround Green Bay 's starting quarterback.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler provided insight into how the Packers and other teams around the league are viewing the Falcons with Michael Penix Jr. back in the lineup.

Micheal Penix Jr. returns against the Green Bay Packers

"Rival teams that have studied them believe that the return of Michael Penix should settle down the offense a bit," wrote the NFL insider.

"One Packers player I spoke to anticipates Atlanta gets Penix acclimated with some easy completions and by leaning on the running game with Bijan Robinson ."

Atlanta named Penix Jr. its starting quarterback on Monday after he completed his recovery from the ACL injury he suffered last season. The Falcons have struggled to generate much offensively, including difficulty establishing Robinson as a consistent part of the rushing attack. Penix showed encouraging signs during his nine appearances in 2025, throwing for 1,982 yards with nine touchdowns and three interceptions. Atlanta now expects the 26 year old to provide more consistency while giving the offense greater potential.

Green Bay will get a close look at how Atlanta responds with Penix back in the lineup, especially with the Packers coming off a short week. The Falcons and Packers will meet at Lambeau Field on Sept. 24 at 8:15 p.m. ET.
