articles.title: Unusual Jets stat offer needed early-season optimism
articles.summary: This stat really puts the Jets' improvements from last season into picture.
articles.body:
One of the things that makes the NFL season what it is is the fact that teams can never get too high or too low.

That's exactly what the New York Jets are experiencing. The heartbreaking 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers is already in the past as head coach Aaron Glenn prepares his team for a Week 3 trip to tackle the Detroit Lions , where he'll face a team he once helped lead after spending four seasons as their defensive coordinator.

The Jets don't have much time to dwell on what happened Sunday, but we do have a moment to look back at two bizarre and surprisingly encouraging statistics that emerged from the home opener.

ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter pointed out that New York ran 55 plays with the lead during its Week 1 victory over the Tennessee Titans . He states, for perspective, the Jets ran just 66 total plays with a lead during all of the 2025 season.

Think about that for a moment. After one game, the Jets had already been ahead for nearly as many offensive snaps as they were during the entirety of the previous season.

Not to be outdone, there is another stat for more context here, noting that the Jets have now run more plays with a lead through two games this season than they did during all of 2025.

That's not going to make the Packers loss any less frustrating, but it does provide another indication that this Jets team is operating from a much different position than last year's group.

The Jets are finding themselves in unfamiliar territory

The second statistic is even more interesting when viewed through the lens of what happened against Green Bay . The Jets led the Packers 17-7 in the fourth quarter and ultimately lost. That is obviously the part everyone remembers, but there is another side to it: New York keeps putting itself in position to control games.

For a team that struggled so badly to play from ahead last season, the early-season transformation is striking. The Jets have not figured out how to consistently finish those games yet, but they are putting themselves in the position to have that problem in the first place.

None of this will help the Jets win Sunday in Detroit. It won't erase the fourth-quarter collapse against Green Bay, either. Still, after the emotional toll of Week 2, we'll take our silver linings wherever we can find them.

articles.title: Climate emergency declaration scrapped by Calderdale Council
articles.summary: Two members of the public are removed from the gallery during the Calderdale Council debate.
articles.body:
Calderdale Council has voted to scrap its climate emergency declaration several years after it was introduced.

The decision was made by the Reform UK-led administration, despite its leader Dan Sutherland having proposed the original declaration when he was a Labour councillor in 2019, saying immediate action was needed.

Protesters gathered outside Halifax Town Hall before Wednesday's meeting, with two members of the public removed from the gallery during the debate.

Reform councillor Connor Dent told the meeting scrapping the declaration was not because "we should care less about our environment", but questioned whether it gave "the best possible outcomes" for residents and the environment.

During the meeting, a 90-year-old protester was among those escorted out by security staff after shouting that scientists had said there was a climate emergency and it should not be ignored.

After another two interruptions, the public gallery was ordered to be cleared, but eventually remaining members of the public were allowed to stay on the basis that they would not further interrupt the debate.

The decision in Calderdale follows similar moves by other Reform-led councils , including Wakefield, which recently voted to "undeclare" the climate emergency the authority had unanimously backed in 2019.

Outlining Calderdale's proposals, Dent said every pound spent by the council must be justified, and environmental policy must deliver real benefits and not just look good on paper.

He said changes shaped by the policy, including building cycle lanes, had caused congestion and a loss of parking spaces which residents had questioned.

He added that the expected increases in the level of cycling had not materialised.

Dent also said the policy had "disconnected" from local worries, citing a battery energy storage plant being given planning permission at Holmfield in Halifax.

Supporting him, Reform councillor Mike Payne said practical, proportionate, safe environmental measures that benefited residents would be supported, but not "virtue signalling".

Opposing the motion, Labour councillor Scott Patient said Reform-led councils were following the party line.

He said the declaration had helped secure £150m for projects, including home insulation, flood resilience and public buildings, and argued that any savings from scrapping it would be minimal.

Supporting him, Councillor Martin Hey, leader of the Green Party group, said that climate initiatives had helped create a green economy worth millions of pounds, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service .

Before the meeting, councillors were lobbied by residents and groups, including Green New Deal and Extinction Rebellion, who voiced concerns about the council's withdrawal from the commitment.

One campaigner, Ali Bath, from Extinction Rebellion, said the previous administration had tried to tackle the issue, but that was now under threat.

She added: "There are huge impacts on our everyday lives and I don't know how communities are going to cope. I don't think people are prepared."

articles.title: Falcons and Packers both searching for answers heading into 'Thursday Night Football' in NFL Week 3
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. takes over for Cooper Rush as the Falcons try to unlock Bijon Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts in a stalling offense.
articles.body: Week 3 is here in the NFL, and I really hope it is nothing like Week 2. Let’s toss aside the sports betting aspect for a moment, but we saw three young quarterbacks- Caleb Williams, Jaxon Dart, and Jayden Daniels- get injured. Timetables are uncertain for some returns, but either way, football is better with primary quarterbacks available. We have two in tonight's game between the Falcons and Packers. The Atlanta Falcons are getting back a starting quarterback of their own. Well… kind of. They are getting Michael Penix Jr. back, but he is returning and taking over for Cooper Rush. The original starter was supposed to be Tua Tagovailoa, but he’s been unavailable all season. Penix Jr. will have his hands full trying to figure out what to do with this offense. They don’t lack playmakers - Bijan Robinson is solid, Drake London is a really good receiver, and Kyle Pitts (although drafted too high) is still a solid option. In the first two games, the Falcons were essentially outmatched. Is that because Rush was under center? In game one, they scored 13 points, but last week they could only get 3 points against a team that almost allowed 60 points in Week 1. The offense wasn’t terrible by some measures - they had 17 first downs, one fewer than the Panthers. However, they had three turnovers; if they shore those up, maybe it’s a more competitive game. MICHAEL PENIX JR. OFFICIALLY NAMED FALCONS STARTER FOR A SHORT-WEEK TRIAL BY FIRE AGAINST PACKERS On the other side of the field is a team with more than enough questions of their own. The Packers are 1-1, but it wasn’t easy to get that victory. They had to go into New Jersey to face the Jets, and they were forced into an overtime game with them. They came out on top 20-17. I don’t want to act like we should be impressed or pleased with that performance, but perhaps it is something to build on, and now they get their first home game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! In Week 1 it wasn’t much better for the Packers. Green Bay was fine against the Vikings, at least for the first half of the game. They struggled to get much going against the Minnesota defense and gave up their lead in the second half. It wasn’t just that; they barely could score and couldn’t keep Carson Wentz from marching down the field. I do blame the front office. I’m not exactly sure that Jordan Love is an elite quarterback, but his receiving options certainly don’t help make him much better. Couple that with Josh Jacobs being out, and this offense should be expected to struggle. articles.title: Hundreds turn out for Bristol's Jacob Elordi lookalike contest
articles.summary: The contest, organised by a group from the University of Bristol, included an Australian accent round.
articles.body:
Hundreds of people turned out to watch a Jacob Elordi lookalike contest which saw youngsters don their finest tote bags and slouchy sweatshirts.

The event, which took place on College Green, was organised by Overheard at UoB - a social media community dedicated to life at the University of Bristol.

Acclaimed Australian actor Elordi is best known for his roles in The Kissing Booth, Saltburn, Frankenstein, Wuthering Heights, Priscilla and the HBO series Euphoria.

Despite some worthy competitors performing their best catwalk struts and Australian accents, the title was awarded to a 17-year-old girl who did not want to be named.

An estimated 500 people showed up to watch the contest unfold.

Jamie Crook, who recently moved to the city from Oxford, said he was shocked at the large turnout and "had jelly legs the whole time".

He said: "I loved it, it was so fun. I'm still kind of shaking now.

"I think it's a really good way to make friends and get to know people.

"I feel like one of the most famous blokes in Bristol for a day, which is an experience."

Mayor believes mass transit system is coming

Hovis workers pause strike after fresh pay deal

The veterinary medicine student even took the time to thank his doppelganger directly, acknowledging the boost to his street cred.

"For the better half of seven years, since the Kissing Booth came out, Jacob Elordi has carried my dating career," he laughed.

"Every time he cuts my hair I show him a picture of Jacob Elordi and he just sorts it out.

Crook explained the accent round was his downfall.

He blamed his croaky impersonation on a lingering "fresher's flu".

Joey Lush secured second place in the competition after trawling through Pinterest for outfit inspiration and "grabbing a tote bag from the fresher's fair".

He said: "He's a very stylish guy, so I tried my best.

"I did not realise what I was signing up for - I was a bit nervous going up."

"The winner did an amazing job," he said. "I'm so okay with it, I lost fair and square.

"I saw her in the line and she was the only one I wouldn't have been... hurt about losing to.

"I think it was her moustache that sold it."

articles.title: PGA Tour Golfer's Caddie Who Quit Mid-Round Explains Reason for Dramatic Split
articles.summary: During the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship in Asheville last week, fans witnessed a live breakup between a golfer and caddie.
articles.body:
During the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship in Asheville last week, fans witnessed a live breakup between a golfer and caddie.

Alejandro Tosti's caddie, Cliff Ellis, dropped his bag, removed his caddie bib and left on the 18th hole of the first round.

While the two reportedly had been at odds before the tournament started, Ellis gave a more in-depth answer as to why he left so suddenly.

According to MondayQ's Ryan French , Ellis had frustrations with Tosti regarding their financial arrangement, but there was also tension with how Ellis was treated on the course and in practice.

Ellis told French that during the Charles Schwab Challenge, Tosti instructed him, "Don't do anything unless I tell you," but became angry and used the F-word multiple times when Ellis didn't immediately pull the flag on the 14th hole.

At the Rocket Classic in Detroit, Ellis said Tosti "went crazy" multiple times during the first round. He said Tosti slammed his clubs on the ground and hit penalty-area stakes in anger. Ellis added that Tosti at one point threw his bag and nearly hit him, though Ellis clarified that he didn't believe the throw was targeted towards him.

According to French, Ellis said a PGA Tour official warned Tosti that he could be suspended if he had another outburst like the one he had in Detroit.

Ellis said issues arose between him and Tosti once again in Asheville last week, specifically noting that he faced criticism for where he placed Tosti's bag.

"Are you going to make me walk to the locker room for my clubs?" Ellis recalled Tosti saying.

After a few missed shots during the first round, Ellis said he encouraged Tosti to let the previous mistakes go and focus on the ones ahead. Tosti confronted him about it on the next tee.

"Don't do that again, or I'll get really angry," Ellis recalled Tosti saying.

Later on, after a back-and-forth about Ellis including an umbrella in the golf bag, he said Tosti repeatedly called him a "dumbass."

The boiling point was on the 18th hole, where Ellis threatened to drop the bag multiple times without receiving much of a response from Tosti. Ultimately, Ellis decided he was done and told Tosti, "Good luck," as he made his way to the parking lot.

articles.title: Judge unseals files in Josh Jacobs case; record requests can proceed
articles.summary: A judge lifted the order sealing records in the Josh Jacobs case, allowing for potential public access to files.
articles.body:
A Brown County Circuit Court Judge on Sept. 24 lifted his temporary order sealing the records in the Josh Jacobs case and said the legal process should play out.

Green Bay Packers running back Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 in Brown County Circuit Court to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges stemming from a May 23 incident in Hobart with an ex-girlfriend.

Judge Marc Hammer said Wisconsin open records law favors public access, but it will be up to the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department to apply a balancing test between the rights of the public, the defendant and the victim in deciding whether to release records. Parties can then appeal the decision, in which case it will end up back in court.

Hobart/Lawrence Police Chief Michael Renkas said the department denied a number of requests so far based on the temporary order to seal the record. Hammer said his order will be vacated by Sept. 25, and new open records requests can be made.

Jacobs missed Packers games so far this season because he is on the commissioner's exempt list, which means he cannot play or practice with the team. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network/ESPN reported on Sept. 13 that the NFL wants to see security video from the home during the incident before deciding on how long Jacobs should be suspended.

The Press-Gazette and other media filed open records requests for the video and other documents, which were denied under the temporary sealed-records order.

Attorneys for the victim submitted a proposed order permanently sealing the records on Sept. 15, citing state statute and Marsy's Law, which ensures that victims of crime have equal, constitutional rights on the same level as those accused and convicted of crimes. Hammer denied that request, preferring that the process continue under open records law rather than through the criminal case.

The victim, who has not been named, is concerned that personally identifying information could be made public. Hammer suggested such information could be removed without the entire record being sealed.

Jacobs has not requested the record be permanently sealed.

For the battery charge , Hammer on Sept. 10 accepted Jacobs' plea and the mutually recommended fine of $1,000 and court costs. For the criminal damage to property charge, he was ordered to not have contact with the victim, pay restitution, attend counseling and be under supervision for one year.

articles.title: Sex offender bailed to flat near playground
articles.summary: Victims of Zapher Dogen were living close to the 32-year-old, who admitted multiple offences.
articles.body:
A sex offender jailed for taking thousands of pictures of children and using AI software to "nudify" them was repeatedly allowed to return to his home overlooking the playground he targeted.

It meant victims of Zafer Dogan, from Enfield in north London, were living close to the 32-year-old, who admitted multiple offences.

Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley spoke outside Wood Green Crown Court after Dogan was jailed for two years and four months, where Sir Mark criticised the "unfathomable decisions" of the justice system.

"The children should be put first, not the paedophile," he said.

Dogan, who works as a mechanic, previously pleaded guilty to multiple offences, including making indecent images of children.

According to the police, he had taken more than 5,000 pictures, many from his bedroom window.

The mother of a victim under the age of eight described feeling "helpless", adding: "Our lives will never be the same again and I can't do anything about it all because one man exploited my child."

The mother of a teenage victim said it was as if she had been "punched in the gut" when police officers told her what had happened.

She added: "I'm really worried that my daughter's photos are online and other paedophiles have them."

Sir Mark said: "Prosecutors rightly opposed bail on multiple occasions, building on officers' clear assessments of the great risk he posed, and yet bail decisions were ultimately made that prioritised the offender's interests over the safety and the peace of mind of the victims.

"A victim and their family found themselves living in close proximity to a man who had admitted targeting them.

"They were so fearful, they ultimately felt forced to move to distant temporary accommodation, disrupting their lives and disrupting their children's lives, simply to escape being in the neighbourhood of the offender."

He also criticised "some grossly irresponsible technology and AI companies".

He said: "Dogan voyeuristically photographed children known to him before using an AI photo-editing technology to manipulate those images for his own sexual gratification. Companies must do more to prevent their platforms and tools from being used to facilitate sexual offending and harm.

"Innovation cannot come at the expense of public safety, and industry has a clear responsibility to help prevent these technologies being exploited by predators.

"Victims, in this case extremely young children and their families, deserve better from both the tech companies and the criminal justice system."

articles.title: Open de France: Michael Kim leads after 'dream start' as Matt Fitzpatrick impresses on low-scoring day at Le Golf National
articles.summary: English duo Matt Fitzpatrick and Sam Bairstow two behind early leader Michael Kim at Le Golf National; Tommy Fleetwood and Viktor Hovland among the other Ryder Cup stars in action; watch live on Friday from 12.30pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Kim carded eight birdies, including four of his first six holes, to post a bogey-free 63 on a low-scoring opening day and grab a two-shot advantage.

The American - beginning on the back nine - followed successive birdies from the 11th by adding two more from the 14th, then ended a run of pars by picking up a shot at the par-four first.

Kim failed to take advantage of the par-five third but added back-to-back birdies from the fifth to move top of the leaderboard, then doubled his lead over the chasing pack - including Fitzpatrick - by picking up a shot at the par-five ninth.

"Just a dream start," Kim said. "All parts of my game were really good, especially my irons and my putting. I couldn't have asked for a better start."

Fitzpatrick also made a blemish-free start, posting six birdies in a six-under 65, with the Englishman one of seven players sharing second after the opening round.

Thriston Lawrence was within one of the lead until a final-hole bogey dropped him back to six under, with Ryder Cup hopeful Kristoffer Reitan and England's Sam Bairstow also two back.

Australian Jason Scrivener and Italian duo Gerogio De Leo and Matteo Manassero are the others alongside Fitzpatrick in tied-second, with Ryder Cup vice-captain Edoardo Molinar three strokes back on five under.

"Really good day," Fitzpatrick said. "Great start to the week and relatively stress-free, which is always nice - particularly around this golf course."

Viktor Hovland is four off the early lead alongside American Ryan Gerard while Tommy Fleetwood - part of Europe's Ryder Cup-winning team at this venue in 2018 - started with a two-under 69.

Manuel Elvira, who double-bogeyed the 72nd hole to miss out on BMW PGA Championship victory on Sunday, sits second-bottom of the leaderboard after a nine-over 80.

articles.title: NFL Week 3 expert picks for Packers vs. Falcons on TNF
articles.summary: Who are the experts taking in the Packers vs. Falcons in Week 3 primetime showdown?
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers might have needed a 10-point comeback at MetLife Stadium to stun the New York Jets and avoid an 0-2 start just four days ago, but the vast majority of experts picking NFL games still believe the Packers will take down the Atlanta Falcons on "Thursday Night Football" to open Week 3.

A victory would improve the Packers to 2-1 going into a long weekend of rest and recovery. But Matt LaFleur's team has to first take care of business in the home opener at Lambeau Field, and there are no simple victories when a team has as many issues as the Packers appear to have through two weeks. Then again, the Falcons are 0-2, coming off a 31-point loss and on the road during a short week.

A review of the Week 3 expert picks of Packers vs. Falcons on TNF:

Of the six experts at USA Today , five picked the Packers.

From Davis: "The Packers know all too well what it's like to try and endure without your most important players at the start of the season, and they'll still be without OLB Micah Parsons and RB Josh Jacobs . But at least they'll finally be home at Lambeau Field, not the ideal environment for Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. to attempt to salvage what may already be a lost season in Atlanta … Though watching him and his talented offensive mates try should at least be entertaining."

Of the 11 experts at ESPN , all 11 picked the Packers.

Of the five experts at NFL.com , all five picked the Packers.

From Cersosimo: "The Packers, lucky to eke out a victory in New York to avoid falling to 0-2, finally return to beloved Lambeau Field, where they have won each of their last 13 home openers. I have concerns about Jordan Love 's O-line, which just lost starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele for the season and has others banged up (OG Aaron Banks , OT Anthony Belton and backup OL Donovan Jennings ). Love has already taken seven sacks (tied for third-most), faced the fifth-highest pressure rate in the NFL this season (42.3%) and is tied for the most unblocked pressures faced (12), per NFL Pro. How Matt LaFleur game plans for his shorthanded offense against a Falcons defense that ranks first against the run, ninth on third down and in the red zone and has generated pressure on 41.5 percent on dropbacks (seventh in the NFL, per Next Gen Stats) could tell part of Thursday night's story. Not having CB A.J. Terrell hurts Atlanta's chances of slowing Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but having Michael Penix Jr. under center should be a boon for that team. Even if he's still knocking off the rust, this should look like a more competent unit, one that's better-suited to get Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts more involved. These are two flawed teams, and though I think we'll see an improved Falcons outfit, Green Bay has a much-needed home-field edge and a defense that's playing with confidence with budding star Lukas Van Ness at the forefront. Clean up the penalties and this could be a turning point for the Pack."

Of the eight experts at MMQB , all eight picked the Packers.

Of the seven experts at The Athletic , all seven picked the Packers.

Of the seven experts at CBS Sports , six picked the Packers.

From Prisco: "This will be Michael Penix back in at quarterback for the Falcons, who badly need it. The Packers rallied to beat the Jets last week, thanks to the defense. That defense will play well here as well. Jordan Love gets it going if the banged-up line can hold up. I think they will."

Of the nine experts at SB Nation , eight picked the Packers.
